scene_description: A small tiled bedroom with a foreground bed, white shelving and a narrow cabinet against the back wall, two floor lamps, a doorway, and a large white furnishing at right.
initial_target_observations: The initial image shows a dark vertical doorway but no broad visible door leaf. The bed and floor remain unobstructed in front of the doorway, unlike the reference.
candidate_target_observations: A light wood-colored, paneled door leaf is now visible, angled into the room and extending down into the foreground. It resembles the reference door in color and general paneling but is narrower in projection, ends higher in the image, and does not overlap the bed or foreground to the same extent.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The candidate door reads as a single angled leaf near the doorway, though its apparent angle, projected width and foreground reach differ from the reference. The shelving, cabinet and lamps retain a broadly similar arrangement. The candidate bed occupies the foreground, but its position and apparent proportions differ from the reference. RGB images cannot establish actual contact or collision.
new_visible_defects: No clearly new defect is visible; the new door silhouette remains a partial match rather than reproducing the reference's larger foreground occlusion.
other_changes: The cabinet's upper panels appear gray and glass-like in the candidate instead of the initially opaque white panels, closer to the reference's glazed cabinet. The candidate remains flatter and more uniformly gray than the reference, with weaker warm lamp illumination, simplified surfaces, and no comparable mottled floor texture. The viewpoint and framing also differ, with the reference showing a larger door and a more dominant bed foreground.

evidence.description: A broad pale wooden paneled door projects into the room and overlaps the foreground area.
The dark doorway is visible without a comparable broad door leaf.
A paneled wooden leaf appears in the doorway, but has a smaller projected footprint than in the reference.
The narrow cabinet has gray translucent-looking upper panels beside the shelving.
Warm lamp light and a mottled tan floor surface are visible around the door.

uncertainty: The apparent difference in door size and occlusion is partly affected by differing camera framing and perspective. A single view cannot establish the door's true dimensions, hinge connection, mesh contact, or hidden geometry.
